div.div: An isolation-forest score is a normalised path length, not a probability: a window isolated in 3 random splits scores 0.82; one at the average path scores 0.5
E(h(x)) = mean splits needed to isolate the window, over the forest
s = 0.5: E(h) equals c(psi); if all windows sit here, no distinct anomaly
well below 0.5: deep in the crowd -> normal
Why short paths mean anomalous (sketch, two template counts per window): random cuts isolate the odd window (red) in 3 cuts; a window inside the crowd needs many.

Defaults and the threshold [B3]
- each tree is built on a sub-sample of psi = 256 points per tree; the forest has t = 100 trees [6]
- c(n) = 2H(n-1) - 2(n-1)/n with H(i) = ln(i) + 0.5772156649 [7]
- scikit-learn contamination='auto' uses offset -0.5 [8] on the shifted score; a numeric contamination flags that share of the training data. It is your alarm budget, not a property of the data.

Read the score correctly [B3]: 0.82 means 'easy to isolate', not '82 % likely to be a bug'. Train on windows from devices believed healthy, or the forest learns faults as normal. It flags environmental anomalies too, so a second signal decides [C4].

Legend — blue line = the score formula (exact); red square = the worked anomalous window; amber circle + dashed = the s = 0.5 reference; grey dotted = tree height limit; green dots = normal windows. Curve computed from c(256) loaded from constants.json.

Sources — every number is loaded from ../constants.json. [n] = public (real value, cited); [n*] = illustrative (an invented round number of realistic order of magnitude; never a measurement).
[1] iforest_subsample_size_default = 256 points per tree — public; Liu, Ting, Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', ICDM 2008, §3 (psi = 256); scikit-learn IsolationForest documentation, (max_samples='auto' = min(256, n_samples))
[2] iforest_c_256 = 10.24 splits — public; my arithmetic from c(n) = 2H(n-1) - 2(n-1)/n in Liu, Ting, Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', ICDM 2008, Eq. 1
[3] iforest_height_limit_psi256 = 8 splits — public; ceil(log2 256); Liu, Ting, Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', ICDM 2008, §3; scikit-learn IsolationForest documentation, (max depth ceil(log2 n))
[4] iforest_score_3_splits_psi256 = 0.82 score — public; my arithmetic: 2^(-3/10.24), from Liu, Ting, Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', ICDM 2008, Eq. 2
[5] iforest_score_at_average_path = 0.5 score — public; Liu, Ting, Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', ICDM 2008, §2: E(h(x)) -> c(n) gives s -> 0.5
[6] iforest_trees_default = 100 trees — public; Liu, Ting, Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', ICDM 2008, §3 (t = 100); scikit-learn IsolationForest documentation, (n_estimators=100)
[7] euler_mascheroni = 0.5772156649 dimensionless — public; Liu, Ting, Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', ICDM 2008, §2, approximation H(i) ~ ln(i) + 0.5772156649
[8] sklearn_iforest_offset_auto = -0.5 score offset — public; scikit-learn IsolationForest documentation, (offset_ = -0.5 when contamination='auto')
